Check a job, run it in the background, and wait for its own checks

Source: R/run-job.R
run_job.Rd

Starts a job the way a long fit should be started, and tells you at once if it is going to fail. Before it submits anything, run_job() checks the things that otherwise fail minutes or hours in: that this session's R is the one the study's renv.lock records, that the packages the job needs are installed at the versions locked, that Quarto can be found, that the job is not already running, and that no other job is rendering in the same study (Quarto allows one render per study). Every failure is listed with how to fix it, and nothing is started until all of them are cleared.

Then it submits the job with submit_job and waits for the render's own checks, the R it runs on and, where the job calls guard_memory, the memory its fit needs. Those can only run inside the render. If one fails, the diagnosis is printed here rather than left in a log.

Usage

run_job(path, final = FALSE, wait = 300, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Character(1). The job's .qmd file.

final

Logical(1). Passed to submit_job.

wait

Numeric(1), seconds, at least 0. How long to wait for the render's own checks. 0 submits and returns at once.

quiet

Logical(1). TRUE prints nothing: not the checks, the note for a legacy job, or the lines the wait ends on. A refusal is still an error, and its message then lists the failed checks and their fixes.

Value

Invisibly, the job's status, as job_status returns it. A job refused by the checks is an error and returns nothing.

Details

A job scaffolded before the setup consolidation has no in-render checks to wait for. run_job() says so and names upgrade_job(), which adds them. The wait ends early when the render finishes, fails or is cancelled. If the checks have not all reported when wait runs out, the render carries on regardless; follow it with job_status. Stop it with cancel_job. Not available on Windows, as for submit_job.

See also

submit_job, job_status, cancel_job, guard_memory

Examples

# Not run by check: it would start a real render.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_job("analyses/nb.boostmtree.lvef.boost.qmd")
} # }
